panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Prometheus reaching the chrony exporter on srv-n2

panels.title: Chrony
panels.description: The exporter answering on chronyd's command port — 0 also means a command was refused

panels.title: Stratum
panels.description: The pool wants stratum 2 or 3; 10 means chronyd fell back to its own clock

panels.title: Clients in log
panels.description: Distinct addresses chronyd is still holding in its client log

panels.title: Rate limited
panels.description: Share of requests dropped by `ratelimit interval 1 burst 16`

panels.title: NTP bandwidth
panels.description: Both directions, counted by netfilter on udp/123

panels.title: Traffic, 30d
panels.description: Prometheus keeps 90d, so this is empty until the counters have that much history

panels.title: Projected month
panels.description: Last 24h extrapolated to 30 days

panels.title: Mean packet
panels.description: 76 bytes over IPv4 and 96 over IPv6 for a plain request; a jump means NTS or an amplification attempt

panels.title: Requests, answers and drops
panels.description: Chrony's own counters, so this is what reached the daemon rather than what hit the NIC

panels.title: Bandwidth by family and direction
panels.description: IP header included, ethernet header not — add roughly 14 bytes a packet for the real link cost

panels.title: Mean packet size
panels.description: Responses larger than requests are how monlist-style amplification shows up

panels.title: Traffic split, last 24h
panels.description: How much of the pool load arrives over IPv4 against IPv6

panels.title: Dropped requests
panels.description: A steady floor is normal for a pool member; a spike is one client hammering

panels.title: Client log records dropped
panels.description: Above zero means clientloglimit is too small and the client stats are truncated

panels.title: Drops per client
panels.description: Cumulative: clients whose dropped-request count is at or below each bound

panels.title: Mean poll interval
panels.description: Averaged over every client chronyd has measured an interval for

panels.title: Polling every 60 s or faster
panels.description: Well-behaved clients poll far slower than this

panels.title: Clients by protocol
panels.description: nts counts clients that finished an NTS-KE handshake, ntp is everyone else

panels.title: Poll interval distribution
panels.description: Rows are seconds between requests, colour is how many clients sit in that band

panels.title: Time since last request
panels.description: Long tails are stale log records rather than live clients

panels.title: Reference
panels.description: The upstream chronyd is currently steering to

panels.title: Maximum clock error
panels.description: The bound chrony documents: |offset| + root dispersion + half the root delay

panels.title: Frequency and skew (ppm)
panels.description: How far the local oscillator runs from true, and chrony's confidence in that figure

panels.title: Receive timestamp source
panels.description: Kernel timestamps are the accurate ones; a VM will never report hardware timestamps

panels.title: Interleaved responses
panels.description: Clients in interleaved mode, which lets them use our transmit timestamps

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: The four upstreams pinned in modules/ntp.nix — losing them all drops us to stratum 10

panels.title: Sample spread per source
panels.description: Standard deviation of the samples chrony kept — network jitter to that upstream

panels.title: Reachability
panels.description: Fraction of the last eight polls that got an answer

panels.title: NTP share of link
panels.description: Pool traffic against everything else this box moves

panels.title: Counter freshness
panels.description: Age of the netfilter dump; the timer rewrites it every 30s
